title: nourishing shattering uruguayan casserole
description: a post-workout, winey, shattering, uruguayan dish featuring tomato sauce and en-croute, perfect for individual-mini-cocotte servings
instructions: in a pan over medium heat, cook the ground beef until browned, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks.
add the onion, garlic, and red bell pepper to the pan and cook until the vegetables are softened.
stir in the chili powder, paprika, salt, and black pepper.
add the canned diced tomatoes and tomato paste to the pan and stir to combine.
in a separate bowl, mix together the feta cheese and a pinch of salt.
grease six individual-mini-cocotte vessels with olive oil.
divide the meat mixture among the vessels, then top each with a spoonful of the feta cheese mixture.
cover the vessels with foil and bake for 20 minutes.
remove the foil and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the feta cheese is golden brown and the casserole is bubbly.
serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley, if desired.
let the casserole rest for a few minutes before serving, allowing the juices to redistribute and the feta cheese to set.
be careful when removing the casserole from the oven, as the cheese will be molten and the vessels may be hot to the touch.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
